faq.q: How do bears get ready for winter?
faq.a: In late summer and autumn bears enter a feeding frenzy, eating huge amounts of berries, nuts, roots and fish, sometimes over 20,000 calories a day, and can gain a third or more of their body weight in fat.
asks: Why do bears eat so much in autumn?

faq.q: How slow is a hibernating bear's heart?
faq.a: A bear's heart can slow from around 50 beats a minute to under 10, with long pauses between beats. Its metabolism drops to about a quarter of its normal rate.
asks: Does a bear's heart slow in winter?
How much energy does a hibernating bear use?

faq.a: For a long time people argued, because a bear's body cools only a few degrees and it can wake fairly quickly. But its metabolism slows hugely for months, so most scientists now call it true hibernation.
asks: Why does a bear stay warm while hibernating?
Is a bear's winter sleep the same as a hedgehog's?

faq.q: Do bears pee when they hibernate?
faq.a: No. Hibernating bears can go months without urinating or passing droppings. Their bodies recycle urea, the main waste in urine, into new proteins that help keep their muscles.
asks: How do bears deal with waste in winter?
Why don't hibernating bears need the toilet?

faq.q: Do bears have babies while hibernating?
faq.a: Yes. Mother bears give birth in the den in midwinter to tiny, hairless cubs, then feed them milk for months while still not eating themselves, all on stored fat.
asks: How do mother bears feed cubs in winter?

facts: During hibernation a black bear's metabolism can fall to about 25 percent of normal while its body temperature drops only a few degrees.
Hibernating bears recycle urea into protein and can go months without urinating.

quiz.say: How is a bear's hibernation different from a hedgehog's?
quiz.show: Compared with a hedgehog, a hibernating bear…
quiz.why: A bear's body stays fairly warm, though its metabolism slows hugely.

wrong.1: Hedgehogs cool to near nest temperature; bears do not.
wrong.2: Bears do not eat at all while hibernating.
